classification.difficultyReason: Unscaffolded: choose the angle opposite the diagonal, cosine rule, then use co-interior angles.

content.prompt:
A parallelogram $JKLM$ has sides $JK=ML=6.5\text{ m}$ and $KL=JM=4.2\text{ m}$.
The diagonal $JL$ is $9\text{ m}$. Find the size of $\angle KJM$, correct to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
Find $\angle JKL$ first.
$$\begin{align*}\cos\angle JKL&=\frac{6.5^2+4.2^2-9^2}{2(6.5)(4.2)}\\\cos\angle JKL&=-\frac{21.11}{54.6}\\\angle JKL&=\cos^{-1}\!\left(-\frac{21.11}{54.6}\right)\\\angle JKL&\approx112.7^\circ\end{align*}$$
$JM\parallel KL$, so co-interior angles sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle KJM&=180^\circ-\angle JKL\\\angle KJM&\approx67^\circ\end{align*}$$
